findingDetails.title: The Bladebro teardown runbook hardcodes one of two data roots, drops the packet's named-session precondition, and cannot verify its own pass criterion
findingDetails.scopeProof: the runbook and the reference it contradicts are both in reviewScopeFiles
findingDetails.case: an operator whose bladebro doctor reported ~/.blade runs BB-014 as written; rm -rf ~/.local/state/blade removes nothing, command -v bladebro prints absent, and the operator records PASS while the real data root and its named sessions are still on disk
findingDetails.claim: BB-014 hardcodes one of two documented data roots, omits the named-session precondition its own reference requires, and has no command that verifies the data root is gone.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: read the whole BB-014 file and the whole install-and-verify.md: no earlier step reads the doctor output and no later step checks the data root. rg for 'data root' and 'named sessions' across mcp-bladebro found install-and-verify.md:77 as the only other statement, and it says the opposite. The recorded macOS run marks BB-014 SKIP.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the hardcoded path could be a deliberate simplification for the common macOS case, since install-and-verify.md:48 lists ~/.local/state/blade first; that explains the path but not the missing named-session precondition nor the absent verifying command.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if BB-014 is documented as a macOS-only convenience scenario whose pass criterion is the binary check alone, with data-root removal delegated to install-and-verify.md:77.

findingDetails.title: The supply-chain digest scenario reads a release sidecar that no step obtains
findingDetails.scopeProof: both files are in reviewScopeFiles; the missing input is named by the scenario's own command list
findingDetails.case: an operator who wants the sidecar comparison rather than the recorded digest runs BB-003 as written and gets cat: <scratch>/sidecar/bladebro-darwin-arm64.sha256: No such file or directory, with no documented step to obtain the file

findingDetails.title: The Aside installer pipes a remote script into bash with no integrity check
findingDetails.scopeProof: the script is a new file added in this branch (git diff --name-status -M reports new file mode 100755)
findingDetails.case: an operator runs scripts/install.sh on a host whose DNS or TLS chain has been subverted; the script executes whatever releases.aside.com returns with the operator's privileges and reports success if the resulting binary answers --version

findingDetails.title: The Chrome DevTools installer suggests running a global npm install under sudo
findingDetails.scopeProof: the script is a new file added in this branch (git diff --name-status -M reports new file mode 100755)
findingDetails.case: an operator hits a permissions error, follows the printed hint, and installs the package as root; every later bdg invocation and every package lifecycle script then runs against a root-owned prefix

results.notes: Decision D5 is implemented on the install side (operator yes required, file never installs itself); the rollback half is where the P1 sits, because the runbook hardcodes the path instead of using the doctor-reported profile directory D5 names.

noveltyJustification: All four findings are new to the run: none appears in the findings registry from iteration 1, and each names a file iteration 1 did not review. Weighted new = 5 (P1) + 3 (P2) = 8 of weighted total 8.
